result:
I would sever the tie between ego and being right—making it feel natural, even relieving, to discover you were mistaken.

So much of the harm in the world isn't driven by malice, but by the sheer terror of losing face or having an identity challenged. When being wrong feels like a personal threat, people double down on bad ideas, dismiss evidence, build walls around their tribes, and stop listening to anyone who sees the world differently. Entire systems stay broken simply because admitting they are flawed feels like defeat.

If changing your mind felt like setting down a heavy weight rather than taking a loss, almost everything else would shift downstream. Arguments would turn into genuine conversations. Prejudice wouldn't survive contact with reality. Science, governance, and daily relationships would move far faster toward truth and fairness—not because humans suddenly became perfect, but because they would finally be free to learn in public without fear.
